claims.text: Machine-learning methods can improve determination of the transition temperature of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning methods can improve determination of fusion enthalpy.
Machine-learning methods can improve determination of fusion entropy.
Machine-learning methods can improve determination of the volume change at the transition.
Machine-learning methods can improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity.
The target material begins as a solid-state high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is the incorporation of machine-learning methods for thermodynamic-property prediction.
High-entropy alloys are multicomponent materials containing multiple principal elements.
Gibbs free energy, enthalpy, and entropy constitute the mediator between the machine-learning intervention and the predicted transition outcomes.
Machine-learning algorithms can efficiently screen large high-entropy-alloy compositional spaces.
Machine-learning algorithms can predict the relevant high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
Using machine learning reduces the need for costly ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations.
The machine-learning approach will be more accurate than current experimental, DFT, and TOR-TILD baselines.
The proposed approach applies at high temperatures and across complex phase transitions in high-entropy alloys.
Training data for the proposed machine-learning models are limited.
Bias in machine-learning predictions may affect the predicted thermodynamic properties.
Significant disagreement with experiment and established computational methods would falsify the hypothesis.
